title: ～合う — do ～ to each other; to fit, to suit
summary: Added to a verb stem, 合う shows that people do the action to each other or together: “～ each other.” On its own, 合う means “to fit, to match, to suit.” Both uses are shown in the examples.

patterns.form: 動詞ます形（語幹） ＋ 合う
patterns.gloss: stem + 合う: 教える → 教え合う (teach each other)

patterns.form: A は B に ＋ 合う
patterns.gloss: A suits B: この色は服に合う

body.p: Verb stem + 合う shows an action that goes both ways or is shared by several people: 話し合う (talk it over), 助け合う (help each other), 出し合う (put in together). It needs two or more people, and they are marked with で or と.

As an independent verb, 合う takes に and means that two things match: 服に合う色 (a color that suits the clothes), 体に合う (suits the body). Do not confuse the two: the stem + 合う combination has a mutual meaning, while the verb 合う alone is about fitness.

examples.ja: クラスのみんなで意見（いけん）を出（だ）し合（あ）いました。
examples.romaji: Kurasu no minna de iken o dashiaimashita.
examples.tr: The whole class exchanged opinions together.

examples.ja: この色（いろ）はあなたの服（ふく）によく合（あ）いますね。
examples.romaji: Kono iro wa anata no fuku ni yoku aimasu ne.
examples.tr: This color really suits your clothes.

examples.ja: 友（とも）だちと連絡先（れんらくさき）を教（おし）え合（あ）った。
examples.tr: My friend and I exchanged contact information with each other.

pitfalls: Use the stem: 教え合う, not 教える合う.
It needs two or more people. For one person acting alone, do not use ～合う.
